QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_26

question.text: State Development Loans (SDLs) are issued by:

explanation.text: The Logic: State Development Loans (SDLs) are government securities issued by state governments and union territories to meet their fiscal requirements. They are part of the broader G-Sec market alongside Central Government Securities. The Trap: Central Government issues dated securities, T-Bills, and special securities — not SDLs. Municipal bonds are separate instruments issued under SEBI regulations. Cross-Exam Context: SDLs are part of the Indian debt market structure tested in Series IV and also relevant for mutual fund portfolios (Series V-A) that invest in G-Secs. Distributor's Pro-Tip: SDLs typically offer a yield premium of 25-75 bps over comparable Central Government Securities, reflecting the slightly higher perceived risk.
